question: Who Owns Hooters?
quick_answer: Hooters' ownership changed in 2025. Hooters of America filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2025 and agreed to hand its company-owned restaurants to a franchisee group that includes some of the brand's original founders. Before that, Hooters of America had been owned by investment firms Nord Bay Capital and TriArtisan Capital Advisors. Hooters was founded in 1983 in Clearwater, Florida.
key_facts: Founded by a group known as the 'Hooters Six'

body.heading: Who owns Hooters now?
body.text: In March 2025, Hooters of America filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to restructure its debts. As part of the plan, the company agreed to sell its company-owned restaurants to a franchisee group that includes some of Hooters' original founders, who already operate many of the brand's franchised locations. In effect, the brand is being handed back toward founder-led ownership.

body.heading: Who owned Hooters before?
body.text: Before the 2025 bankruptcy, Hooters of America was owned by two investment firms, Nord Bay Capital and TriArtisan Capital Advisors, which had acquired it around 2019. The bankruptcy was driven by debt and tougher conditions for casual-dining chains, not by the brand disappearing.

body.heading: The brand's roots
body.text: Hooters opened its first restaurant in 1983 in Clearwater, Florida, started by a group of six businessmen often called the 'Hooters Six.' The founders' group that is taking over company restaurants is tied to that original ownership lineage.

faqs.a: Yes. Hooters of America filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2025 to restructure its debt. It is being reorganized, with company-owned restaurants moving to a founder-led franchisee group.
